introduction-stop-grepping-production.core: SSH-ing into servers to grep logs doesn't scale and disappears with ephemeral instances. CloudWatch centralises logs and metrics: Logs Insights queries across log groups, metric filters turn log patterns into metrics, and alarms (including composite alarms) notify and act on signals.

first_principles.problem: During an incident, engineers log into 30 instances to grep logs that may already be gone.
truths: Central logs are queryable at once.
Metrics are cheaper to alert on than raw logs.
derivation: **Ship logs** to CloudWatch (agent, awslogs driver, Lambda).
**Extract metrics** with metric filters or EMF.

analogy.title: A central security control room
analogy.story: All camera feeds in one place, with motion alerts, instead of walking to each camera.
analogy.breaks: Cameras record visually; logs need structure to be queryable.

example.title: Incident triage
flow: After: one Insights query across all services

check.a: Fields become queryable and filterable in Logs Insights and metric filters.

cloudwatch-logs-insights.core: Logs Insights is a purpose-built query language over log groups: fields, filter, parse, stats (count, avg, pct), sort and limit, with auto-discovered JSON fields. It's billed per GB scanned, so narrow time ranges and log groups. Saved queries and dashboard widgets make investigations repeatable.

first_principles.problem: Engineers can't compute p99 latency or top error endpoints from raw logs quickly.

analogy.title: A spreadsheet pivot table over your logs
analogy.story: Filter, group and summarise in seconds.
analogy.breaks: Spreadsheets hold small data; Insights scans gigabytes per query and bills for it.

code.text:
fields @timestamp, route, latency_ms
| filter status >= 200
| stats pct(latency_ms, 99) as p99, count(*) as n by route, bin(5m)
| sort p99 desc
| limit 20

check.a: By the amount of log data scanned per query.

metric-filters-logs-to-metrics.core: Metric filters watch incoming log events for patterns (terms or JSON field conditions) and publish CloudWatch metrics, such as a count of ERROR lines or the value of a latency field. Alarms can then fire on those metrics. The Embedded Metric Format (EMF) lets apps emit metrics inside structured logs directly.

first_principles.problem: A team wants an alert when payment failures exceed 10 per minute, but only has logs.
truths: Alarms work on metrics, not raw logs.
Patterns can be matched as logs arrive.
Metrics are cheap to store and alert on.

analogy.title: A tally counter clicked whenever a word appears in the transcript
analogy.story: You watch the counter, not the whole transcript.
analogy.breaks: Tally counters can be reset; metric filters only count events ingested after creation.

check.q: Do metric filters apply to logs ingested before the filter was created?
check.a: No; they only process new log events.

composite-alarms.core: Composite alarms combine other alarms with boolean logic (AND, OR, NOT) into one actionable signal, e.g. page only if errors are high AND latency is high, or suppress alarms during deployments. They cut alert noise and alert fatigue while keeping underlying alarms for dashboards.

first_principles.problem: On-call receives 15 pages for one incident because every related alarm fires separately.

analogy.title: A smoke detector that only sounds when both smoke and heat are present
analogy.story: Fewer false alarms from burnt toast.
analogy.breaks: Fire detectors react instantly; composite alarms depend on child alarm evaluation periods.

code.text: ALARM("api-5xx-high") AND (ALARM("api-p99-high") OR ALARM("checkout-fail-high")) AND NOT ALARM("deploy-in-progress")

check.q: How do composite alarms reduce alert fatigue?
check.a: They combine related symptoms into one signal and only notify when the combined condition holds.
